voices.line: I'd love to learn what Emma does. Would you ask them?
If you pass Mia, would you ask how they are? I'd like to know.
Emma's a patient teacher.
Can I tell you something about the evening Noah and Leo spent at Anchor Pub? I've a soft spot for it, if I'm honest.
Sat on the bench and let the sea do the talking.
Here's something about the spring tides I've never said. Twice a month the sea comes right up to the doors.
Best cider in years. Every bit as good as last year.
You'll wear that bench out, moving it about.
I can't be in a room with Olek. Not after a letter that never came.
A crab tried to share the bench with me. I let it.
We talked, Olek and me. It's better.
I'm done with Lise.
Funny, we've never talked about the otters. If you see one, don't tell anyone. They like their peace.
I've never told you about Sofia, have I? We get on well enough.
Aye. The bench by the harbour now? Aye, I see it.
I've never told you what I think of the day Hana and Lise fell out. It means more to me than I let on.
Can I tell you something about the ginger cat? They know when the boats come in before we do.
I've never told you what I think of the Midwinter Feast. It means more to me than I let on.
Did you see it go up? Every bit as good as last year.
Now the bench's by Anchor Pub, I'll sit there.
You'll know Olek by now. We nod in passing. That's about it.
Noah knows what they did.
I'd love to learn what Mara does. Would you ask them? Maeve sends their love.
Here we are again. Last time round, work went on at a new net loft over the quay. The old one leans. One more gale and it lies down.
It's taking shape, isn't it?
Can I tell you something about the evening Hana and Mara spent at the harbour? My mother loved it. So do I.
We've finished the new net loft over the quay! How shall we open it?
Same as before, I'm afraid. Last time round, Noah had a birthday party. My birthday, if anyone's counting.
Every child should have a shelf of their own to choose from.
A splendid do. Thank you all.
The bench by the harbour now? Aye, I see it.
You've never heard me on the school play, have you? I've a soft spot for it, if I'm honest.
The children cut the ribbon. Twice.
Fair enough.
I can't be in a room with Hana. Not after the regatta.
Can I tell you something about the old boat names? Every boat is named for someone. Some for someone's mother-in-law.
Half the harbour came to watch today.
Never seen so many friends round one table. Every bit as good as last year.
We talked, Hana and me. It's better.
Oh, you've moved it. It suits there.
I can't be in a room with Hana. Not after the goat in the garden.
We talked, Hana and me. It's better. Still not speaking to Hana.
Must look Ivo up sometime.
Did I ever tell you about Maeve? I'd trust them with anything.
I'd love to learn what Jonas does. Would you ask them?
Here's something about the evening Sofia and Ada spent at Anchor Pub I've never said. I remember the first time, clear as day.
Jonas's a patient teacher. Home to Ada now.
Hm. The bench by the harbour now? Aye, I see it.
I can't remember my last day off.
I've never told you what I think of the Blossom Walk. It means more to me than I let on.
Frost on the nets. Winter's here. Every bit as good as last year.
A whole day off. I'd forgotten what that was.
I've never told you what I think of Spring Clean. It always puts me in a good mood.
If you see Noah, would you tell them I'm sorry? I can't find the words myself.
The bench again? Anchor Pub it is, then.
I'd love to learn what Jonas does. Would you ask them? Emma sends their love.
Can I tell you something about Sofia? We nod in passing. That's about it.
The fog rolled in while I sat on the bench. Cosy, somehow.
Jonas's a patient teacher. Emma sends their love.
Rosa's a proper friend.
I've never told you what I think of the day Mara began teaching Lise. My mother loved it. So do I.
I don't think I've said a word about the mainland news before. It's always a week late here. It never matters.
Read the paper on the bench. All of it, even the tides.
The bench by the harbour now? Aye, I see it.
There's a dip in the bench just my shape now.
Standing ovation! Every bit as good as last year.
I don't think I've said a word about the market bell before. It's cracked. It still does the job.
Waved at every boat from the bench. Most waved back.
Same as before, I'm afraid. Last time round, Evan had a birthday party. Another year older. Still got all my fingers.
Now that was a party.
Someone's fond of moving that bench.
I feel stuck. Jonas could teach me a thing or two. Ada is a gem.
I've been meaning to say something about Emma. One of the best people I know.
The bench creaks like an old hull. I like that.
Here we are again. Last time round, work went on at a library corner for the school. Every child should have a shelf of their own to choose from.
Half the harbour came to watch today.
Ivo said sorry. So did I.
You've never heard me on the evening Mara and Noah spent at Anchor Pub, have you? It means more to me than I let on.
We've finished the library corner for the school! How shall we open it?
Scones, a pot of tea and the whole sea to look at.
Everyone came. Even the gulls.
I don't think I've said a word about the tide clock before. Everything waits on the tide. Even weddings.
Dozed on the bench and woke to the ferry's horn.
Coming along nicely.
The bench by the harbour now? Aye, I see it.
Maybe next month.
Funny, we've never talked about the island's dogs. Old Bess walks the quay at six every morning. Nobody owns her.
Watched the tide turn from the bench. It took its time.
Everyone came. Everyone. Every bit as good as last year.
Did I ever tell you about Tobias? We get on well enough.
Better there, I think.
Can I tell you something about the evening Maeve and Jonas spent at Anchor Pub? I've a soft spot for it, if I'm honest.
The bench by the harbour catches the last of the sun.
I hardly see Olek these days.
I've never told you what I think of the Blossom Walk. I remember the first time, clear as day.
Wrote to my sister from the bench. Told her about the gulls.
Here's something about the shells on the beach I've never said. Every storm brings new ones. The children count them.
Round the buoy and home first! Every bit as good as last year.
The bench looks at home by the harbour.
Mara makes it look easy. Could I learn from them?
I've never told you about Lise, have I? We nod in passing. That's about it.
Mara's a patient teacher.
Can I tell you something about the evening Mara and Emma spent at the harbour? It always puts me in a good mood.
Can I tell you something about the harbour wall? Stand on it in a gale and you feel it shake.
Same as before, I'm afraid. Last time round, Sofia had a birthday party. It's my birthday. I want nothing. Well, maybe cake.
A party! I didn't expect that.
By Anchor Pub, the bench? Suits it.
Funny, we've never talked about the harbour's colours. Blue doors, red boats and white walls. That's us.
I've been meaning to say something about Emma. We nod in passing. That's about it.
I don't think I've said a word about the evening Olek and Rosa spent at the harbour before. My mother loved it. So do I.
Freezing! Best thing ever! Every bit as good as last year.
Well. The bench by the harbour now? Aye, I see it.
Here's something about the school play I've never said. I could take it or leave it, to be fair.
Have you seen Maeve lately? Would you look in on them for me?
You've never heard me on the old postmistress, have you? She kept sweets under the counter for the children.
Here we are again. Last time round, work went on at tea rooms on the pier. Scones, a pot of tea and the whole sea to look at.
Coming along nicely.
I'll miss the gulls. Not the wind.
The weaving shed needs looking after. I'm good at that.
Mia and I used to be close.
We've finished the tea rooms on the pier! How shall we open it?
Old Mrs Pell can't walk to the bakery any more. The bread can walk to her.
Speeches, cake and everyone in their best!
Round and round goes the bench. I like it here.
I'm Pim, by the way. I've seen you about.
Another part done. Look at that.
Evenings are long on my own.
I've been meaning to say something about Pim. We nod in passing. That's about it.
We've finished the bread cart for the far cottages! How shall we open it?
Summer evenings outside, with the sea right there.
Bunting up and the whole harbour here!
A year ago today, Leo spent an evening at Anchor Pub with Emma. I still think about it.
Mackerel running thin off the old wreck.
Sorted the back room at Harbour Bakery. Found a ghost. Probably a cat.
Little Ada asked about seabirds. I'll be up till ten. Home to Ada now. Class dismissed.
Counted the boats in. All home, thank goodness. Maeve is a gem.
Mia had me fetching and carrying. Seeing Hana later.
Soap went up for no reason. Ada is a gem.
Lost to Emma again. It's tradition now. Quiet without anyone to talk to.
Potatoes in. Hana lent me a spade. Home to Hana now.
Walked the cliff path with Emma. Home to Jonas now.
Won three hands off Mia! Olek is a gem.
Rushed off our feet at the harbour, Noah and me.
Did the books at the harbour. They nearly balance. Ivo sends their love.
Slugs ate my lettuces. Mia says beer traps. Seeing Noah later.
Sold my old things. Hana bought the lamp!
You've never heard me on the day Leo and Hana talked it through, have you? It always puts me in a good mood.
